findings.title: Apache Tomcat embedded (tomcat-embed-core 10.1.46) — multiple Critical/High request-smuggling, auth-bypass and DoS CVEs

locations.note: spring-boot-starter-parent BOM manages the embedded Tomcat version
spring-boot-starter-web pulls in spring-boot-starter-tomcat -> tomcat-embed-core transitively

findings.description: The embedded Apache Tomcat shipped with Spring Boot 3.5.6 (tomcat-embed-core 10.1.46) is affected by 14 CVEs, including three Critical ones: CVE-2026-41293 (HTTP/2 request headers not validated, CVSS 9.8), CVE-2026-43512 (authentication bypass via digest authentication, CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-43515 (improper authorization allows security bypass, CVSS 9.1). High-severity issues include certificate revocation bypass (CVE-2026-24734), HTTP request/response smuggling via invalid chunk extension (CVE-2026-24880), and several information-disclosure and DoS flaws. Trivy reports the package as a transitive (indirect) dependency pulled in via spring-boot-starter-web -> spring-boot-starter-tomcat.
findings.rootCause: tomcat-embed-core version is managed by the spring-boot-starter-parent BOM (declared at pom.xml lines 8-15, version 3.5.6). Boot 3.5.6 pins Tomcat 10.1.46, which predates the 10.1.55 fix line.
findings.impact: Remote, unauthenticated attackers can smuggle/inject HTTP/2 request headers, bypass digest authentication and authorization, bypass certificate revocation checks, and trigger DoS — directly exposing every REST endpoint of the multi-tenant GRC API to request smuggling and auth-bypass attacks against the perimeter servlet container.
findings.reproduction: Build the backend (mvn dependency:tree | grep tomcat-embed-core shows 10.1.46) and run Trivy: `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`. CVE-2026-41293, CVE-2026-43512 and CVE-2026-43515 appear as CRITICAL against tomcat-embed-core 10.1.46.
findings.resolution: Upgrade the spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (the 3.5.x patch line that pins Tomcat >= 10.1.55), or pin the Tomcat version explicitly via the spring-boot.dependencies-managed property <tomcat.version>10.1.55</tomcat.version> in <properties>. Rebuild and re-scan to confirm tomcat-embed-core resolves to >= 10.1.55.
findings.patchAfter:
<parent>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3.5.14</version>
    <relativePath/>
</parent>
<!-- If the Boot bump cannot reach Tomcat 10.1.55, also add in <properties>: -->
<!-- <tomcat.version>10.1.55</tomcat.version> -->

findings.title: Spring Security Web 6.5.5 — HTTP response headers may not be written (security policy bypass & information disclosure)

locations.note: spring-boot-starter-parent BOM manages the Spring Security version
spring-boot-starter-security pulls in spring-security-web transitively

findings.description: spring-security-web 6.5.5 is affected by CVE-2026-22732 (CWE-425, CVSS 9.1): when servlet applications specify HTTP response headers via Spring Security and rely on the default lazy header-writing, there is a possibility that security-relevant HTTP headers are never written to the response, leading to a security policy bypass and information disclosure.
findings.rootCause: Spring Security version is managed by the spring-boot-starter-parent BOM (pom.xml lines 8-15, Boot 3.5.6 pins Spring Security 6.5.5), which predates the 6.5.9 fix.
findings.impact: Security headers (e.g. cache-control, frame options, CSP) configured through Spring Security may silently fail to be written, bypassing the application's intended security policy and disclosing protected information — high risk for a security platform whose own headers harden the bilingual GRC UI and API.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2026-22732 reports CRITICAL against spring-security-web 6.5.5. `mvn dependency:tree` confirms spring-security-web:6.5.5 is pulled by spring-boot-starter-security.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (which pins Spring Security >= 6.5.9/6.5.10) or override <spring-security.version>6.5.10</spring-security.version> in <properties>. Re-scan to confirm spring-security-web and spring-security-core resolve to >= 6.5.10.

findings.title: Microsoft SQL Server JDBC Driver 12.8.1.jre11 — improper input validation enables spoofing (CVE-2025-59250)

locations.note: <mssql.version>12.8.1.jre11</mssql.version> property
direct mssql-jdbc dependency declaration

findings.description: The directly declared mssql-jdbc 12.8.1.jre11 driver is affected by CVE-2025-59250 (CWE-20, CVSS 8.1): improper input validation in the JDBC Driver for SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
findings.rootCause: Explicitly pinned to 12.8.1.jre11 via the <mssql.version> property (pom.xml line 32) and consumed at lines 112-116; the 12.8.2.jre11 patch on the 12.8.x line was not applied.
findings.impact: A network attacker can spoof the database connection path with high confidentiality and integrity impact, undermining the trust boundary between the backend and the multi-tenant SQL Server holding all GRC data.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2025-59250 reports HIGH against com.microsoft.sqlserver:mssql-jdbc 12.8.1.jre11.
findings.resolution: Bump the <mssql.version> property to 12.8.2.jre11 (smallest same-line patch) or a later fixed release (e.g. 12.10.2.jre11). No code changes required; re-run the build and Trivy to confirm.

findings.title: Spring Boot Actuator 3.5.6 — authentication bypass via Health Group additional path & CloudFoundry endpoints

locations.note: direct spring-boot-starter-actuator dependency (version managed by parent BOM lines 8-15)

findings.description: spring-boot-starter-actuator 3.5.6 is affected by CVE-2026-22731 (CWE-288/CWE-306, CVSS 8.2): an authentication-bypass when an authenticated endpoint is declared under a path already configured as a Health Group additional path; and CVE-2026-22733 (CVSS 8.2): authentication bypass under Actuator CloudFoundry endpoints.
findings.rootCause: Actuator starter is declared directly (pom.xml lines 66-69) but its version is managed by spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6 (lines 8-15), which predates the 3.5.12 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-actuator", InstalledVersion "3.5.6", CVE-2026-22731 Severity HIGH, FixedVersion "3.5.12, 4.0.4". pom.xml lines 66-69 declare spring-boot-starter-actuator.
findings.impact: The platform exposes the Actuator (Prometheus scrape and health endpoints, see pom.xml lines 212-218). A misconfigured Health Group additional path could let an unauthenticated caller reach endpoints that should require authentication, leaking operational and security telemetry.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2026-22731 and CVE-2026-22733 report HIGH against spring-boot-starter-actuator 3.5.6.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (>= 3.5.12 contains the Actuator fix). Verify any Health Group additional-path configuration after the upgrade.

findings.title: Spring Boot 3.5.6 — predictable ApplicationTemp directory enables code execution / session hijacking (CVE-2026-40973)

locations.note: spring-boot-starter-parent BOM pins the spring-boot core artifact version

findings.description: The spring-boot core artifact 3.5.6 is affected by CVE-2026-40973 (CWE-377, CVSS 7.0): a local attacker on the same host can take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent=true and the attack persists across restarts, the attacker can read session information to hijack authenticated users, or deploy a gadget chain to execute code as the application user.
findings.rootCause: The spring-boot core version is pinned by spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6 (pom.xml lines 8-15), which predates the 3.5.14 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot", InstalledVersion "3.5.6", CVE-2026-40973 Severity HIGH, FixedVersion "4.0.6, 3.5.14".
findings.impact: On a shared host a local attacker could hijack authenticated GRC sessions or achieve code execution as the application user. Exposure depends on session persistence configuration, but the predictable temp directory is created regardless.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2026-40973 reports HIGH against spring-boot 3.5.6.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (or 4.0.6). As defense-in-depth, avoid setting server.servlet.session.persistent=true and ensure the temp directory is on a path not writable by other local users.

findings.title: Apache POI OOXML 5.2.5 — duplicate zip-entry parsing reads unexpected data (CVE-2025-31672)

locations.note: <poi.version>5.2.5</poi.version> property
direct poi-ooxml dependency declaration

findings.description: poi-ooxml 5.2.5 is affected by CVE-2025-31672 (CWE-20, CVSS 6.9): improper input validation when parsing OOXML files (xlsx, docx, pptx). Because these are zip files, a malicious file with duplicate zip-entry names can cause POI to read different data than the user/validator expects.
findings.rootCause: POI is explicitly pinned to 5.2.5 via the <poi.version> property (pom.xml line 34) and declared at lines 165-169; the 5.4.0 fix was not applied.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.apache.poi:poi-ooxml", InstalledVersion "5.2.5", CVE-2025-31672 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "5.4.0". pom.xml line 34: <poi.version>5.2.5</poi.version>.
findings.impact: The Excel/Office export and any import path that parses uploaded OOXML files could be tricked into reading attacker-controlled hidden entries, enabling data-integrity confusion in GRC report generation.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2025-31672 reports MEDIUM against poi-ooxml 5.2.5.
findings.resolution: Bump the <poi.version> property to 5.4.0 (applies to both poi and poi-ooxml, declared at pom.xml lines 160-169). Re-run the build and Trivy.

findings.title: Jackson Core 2.19.2 — async parser bypasses maxNumberLength leading to DoS (GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq)

locations.note: Jackson BOM version is managed by spring-boot-starter-parent

findings.description: jackson-core 2.19.2 is affected by GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq (CVSS 6.9): the non-blocking (async) JSON parser bypasses the maxNumberLength StreamReadConstraint (default 1000 chars), allowing arbitrarily long numbers that cause excessive memory allocation and CPU exhaustion (DoS).
findings.rootCause: Jackson is pulled transitively (via jjwt-jackson at pom.xml lines 104-109, logstash-logback-encoder at 220-224, and Spring web) with its version managed by the spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6 BOM (lines 8-15), which pins jackson 2.19.2, below the 2.18.6/2.21.1 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core", InstalledVersion "2.19.2", GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "2.21.1, 2.18.6".
findings.impact: Any endpoint or component using Jackson's async parser to read attacker-supplied JSON can be driven to memory/CPU exhaustion, degrading availability of the API.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq reports MEDIUM against jackson-core 2.19.2.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to a release that pins jackson >= 2.21.1 (e.g. Boot 3.5.14 line; verify the managed jackson-bom version after upgrade), or override <jackson-bom.version>2.21.1</jackson-bom.version> in <properties>. Re-scan to confirm.

findings.title: Apache Commons Compress 1.25.0 — unbounded resource allocation / infinite loop DoS (CVE-2024-26308, CVE-2024-25710)

locations.note: commons-compress is pulled transitively by poi-ooxml

findings.description: commons-compress 1.25.0 is affected by CVE-2024-26308 (CWE-770, CVSS 6.7 — OutOfMemoryError unpacking a broken Pack200 file) and CVE-2024-25710 (CVSS 5.9 — infinite loop / DoS on a corrupted DUMP file).
findings.rootCause: commons-compress is an indirect dependency of poi-ooxml (pom.xml lines 165-169) and resolves to 1.25.0, below the 1.26.0 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.apache.commons:commons-compress", InstalledVersion "1.25.0", CVE-2024-26308 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "1.26.0".
findings.impact: Processing a malicious archive (e.g. via the POI-backed import/export paths) can exhaust memory or hang a thread, causing a denial of service.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2024-26308 and CVE-2024-25710 report MEDIUM against commons-compress 1.25.0.
findings.resolution: Force commons-compress >= 1.26.0 via an explicit <dependencyManagement> entry (since it arrives transitively through POI). Bumping <poi.version> to 5.4.0 also upgrades the transitive commons-compress; verify the resolved version with mvn dependency:tree.

findings.title: Apache Commons Lang3 3.17.0 — uncontrolled recursion StackOverflowError DoS (CVE-2025-48924)

locations.note: commons-lang3 version managed transitively via Spring Boot BOM

findings.description: commons-lang3 3.17.0 is affected by CVE-2025-48924 (CWE-674, CVSS 6.5): ClassUtils.getClass(...) can throw StackOverflowError on very long inputs (uncontrolled recursion). Because an Error is usually not caught, this can crash the calling thread.
findings.rootCause: commons-lang3 arrives transitively (managed by the Spring Boot 3.5.6 dependency BOM, pom.xml lines 8-15) at 3.17.0, below the 3.18.0 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.apache.commons:commons-lang3", InstalledVersion "3.17.0", CVE-2025-48924 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "3.18.0".
findings.impact: Code paths that call ClassUtils.getClass on attacker-influenced strings can be forced into a StackOverflowError, terminating the handling thread and degrading availability.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2025-48924 reports MEDIUM against commons-lang3 3.17.0.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (which pins commons-lang3 >= 3.18.0) or add an explicit <dependencyManagement> override to 3.18.0. Re-scan to confirm.

findings.title: Spring Framework WebMVC 6.2.11 — path traversal in script template views & DoS (CVE-2026-22737 + 3 more)

locations.note: Spring Framework version managed by spring-boot-starter-parent
spring-boot-starter-web pulls in spring-webmvc

findings.description: spring-webmvc 6.2.11 is affected by CVE-2026-22737 (CWE-22, CVSS 6.5 — information disclosure via Java scripting-engine template views, files outside configured locations), plus CVE-2026-22745 (DoS via slow static resource resolution on Windows, CVSS 5.3), CVE-2026-22741 (DoS via cache poisoning, CVSS 5.9) and CVE-2026-22735 (SSE stream corruption, CVSS 2.6).
findings.rootCause: Spring Framework version is managed by spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6 (pom.xml lines 8-15), which pins Spring 6.2.11, below the 6.2.17/6.2.18 fixes.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.springframework:spring-webmvc", InstalledVersion "6.2.11", CVE-2026-22737 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "7.0.6, 6.2.17".
findings.impact: If script-template views are enabled, an authenticated user could read files outside the configured template locations; the DoS variants threaten API availability (notably the Windows static-resource path, relevant given this deployment runs on Windows).
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2026-22737/22745/22741/22735 report against spring-webmvc 6.2.11.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (pins Spring Framework >= 6.2.18) or override <spring-framework.version>6.2.18</spring-framework.version> in <properties>. Re-scan to confirm spring-webmvc resolves to >= 6.2.18.

findings.title: Spring Framework WebSocket 6.2.11 — STOMP-over-WebSocket CSRF / security bypass (CVE-2025-41254)

locations.note: spring-boot-starter-websocket pulls in spring-websocket transitively
Spring Framework version managed by parent BOM

findings.description: spring-websocket 6.2.11 is affected by CVE-2025-41254 (CWE-352, CVSS 4.3): STOMP-over-WebSocket applications may be vulnerable to a CSRF-style security bypass that lets an attacker send unauthorized messages.
findings.rootCause: The platform uses STOMP/WebSocket (spring-boot-starter-websocket declared at pom.xml lines 207-210; the comment notes 'Real-time push ... Topics namespaced by org.{orgId}.* for tenant isolation'). spring-websocket version is managed by Spring Boot 3.5.6 BOM (lines 8-15) at 6.2.11, below the 6.2.12 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.springframework:spring-websocket", InstalledVersion "6.2.11", CVE-2025-41254 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "6.2.12".
findings.impact: An attacker could send unauthorized STOMP messages, potentially crossing the per-tenant topic namespace (org.{orgId}.*) used for notifications and lifecycle/SLA pushes, undermining tenant isolation of the real-time channel.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2025-41254 reports MEDIUM against spring-websocket 6.2.11.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (pins Spring Framework >= 6.2.12) or override <spring-framework.version>6.2.18</spring-framework.version> (which also covers SEC-CVE-010). Re-scan to confirm.

findings.title: Logback Core 1.5.18 — conditional arbitrary code execution & arbitrary class instantiation (CVE-2025-11226, CVE-2026-1225)

locations.note: logback version managed by spring-boot-starter-parent BOM
logstash-logback-encoder pairs with the managed logback runtime

findings.description: logback-core 1.5.18 is affected by CVE-2025-11226 (CWE-20, CVSS 6.4): conditional arbitrary code execution when an attacker can compromise a logback configuration file or inject an environment variable (requires Janino + Spring on the classpath); and CVE-2026-1225 (CVSS 5.0): a malicious logback.xml allows instantiation of arbitrary classes.
findings.rootCause: logback-core is an indirect dependency whose version is managed by spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.6 (pom.xml lines 8-15) at 1.5.18, below the 1.5.19 / 1.5.25 fixes.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "ch.qos.logback:logback-core", InstalledVersion "1.5.18", CVE-2025-11226 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "1.5.19, 1.3.16"; CVE-2026-1225 FixedVersion "1.5.25".
findings.impact: An attacker able to tamper with logging configuration (or environment variables consumed by it) could execute code or instantiate arbitrary classes in the backend JVM. Exposure is gated by config-file integrity but raises the impact of any config-write primitive.
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2025-11226 and CVE-2026-1225 report against logback-core 1.5.18.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 (pins logback >= 1.5.19) and, to also cover CVE-2026-1225, override <logback.version>1.5.25</logback.version> in <properties>. Re-scan to confirm logback-core resolves to >= 1.5.25.

findings.title: Spring Security Core 6.5.5 — One-Time-Token TOCTOU race & timing-attack info disclosure (CVE-2026-22751, CVE-2026-22746)

locations.note: spring-boot-starter-security pulls in spring-security-core transitively
Spring Security version managed by parent BOM

findings.description: spring-security-core 6.5.5 is affected by CVE-2026-22751 (CWE-367, CVSS 4.8): a Time-of-check/Time-of-use race in JdbcOneTimeTokenService allows One-Time-Token login authentication bypass; and CVE-2026-22746 (CVSS 3.7): a timing-attack defense bypass allowing information disclosure.
findings.rootCause: spring-security-core is pulled via spring-boot-starter-security (pom.xml lines 58-61) with its version managed by Spring Boot 3.5.6 BOM (lines 8-15) at 6.5.5, below the 6.5.10 fix.
findings.evidence: Trivy: PkgName "org.springframework.security:spring-security-core", InstalledVersion "6.5.5", CVE-2026-22751 Severity MEDIUM, FixedVersion "6.5.10, 7.0.5".
findings.impact: If One-Time-Token login with JdbcOneTimeTokenService is configured, a race condition can be exploited to bypass authentication; the timing-attack flaw can leak information. Same remediation as SEC-CVE-002 (Spring Security upgrade).
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-backend/pom.xml`; CVE-2026-22751 and CVE-2026-22746 report against spring-security-core 6.5.5.
findings.resolution: Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 or override <spring-security.version>6.5.10</spring-security.version> in <properties> (covers SEC-CVE-002 and this finding). Re-scan to confirm spring-security-core resolves to >= 6.5.10.

findings.title: react-router 6.30.3 — open redirect via protocol-relative URL reinterpretation (CVE-2026-40181)

locations.note: react-router 6.30.3 locked entry
react-router-dom ^6.28.0 direct dependency pulls react-router 6.30.3 transitively

findings.description: react-router 6.30.3 is affected by CVE-2026-40181 (CWE-601, CVSS 6.6): URLs passed to the redirect function whose path starts with // are reinterpreted as protocol-relative URLs, triggering an open redirect to an external domain. Affects versions 6.7.0-6.30.3 and 7.0.0-7.14.0 (Framework/Data modes; not Declarative <BrowserRouter>).
findings.rootCause: react-router is locked at 6.30.3 in tss-grc-ui-v2/package-lock.json (lines 2048-2062), pulled transitively by the direct dependency react-router-dom ^6.28.0 declared in tss-grc-ui-v2/package.json line 21. 6.30.3 is below the 6.30.4 fix.
findings.impact: If the React UI returns a redirect built from user-controlled input, an attacker can craft a // path to redirect victims to an external malicious domain (phishing / token theft), since impact depends on the app's pre-redirect validation. Note the same CVE also affects react-router 6.30.3 in TSS-Theme/package-lock.json (line 1611-1625).
findings.reproduction: Run `trivy fs --scanners vuln tss-grc-ui-v2/package-lock.json`; CVE-2026-40181 reports MEDIUM against react-router 6.30.3.
findings.resolution: Bump react-router-dom to ^6.30.4 in tss-grc-ui-v2/package.json (pulls react-router 6.30.4) and run `npm install` to refresh the lockfile. Re-scan to confirm react-router resolves to >= 6.30.4. Apply the same bump to TSS-Theme if it ships to production.
